name: Cathodic protection and coatings (FBE, 3LPE)
principle: A dielectric coating (fusion-bonded epoxy, three-layer polyethylene) keeps most of the pipe from contact with soil, and cathodic protection supplies current through sacrificial anodes or an impressed-current rectifier to cover coating defects. ICCP uses a DC source of up to about 50 A and 50 V depending on pipe size and coating quality.

process_steps.name: Apply external coating at the mill
Install anodes or groundbed and rectifier

performance.metric: ICCP source rating for a pipeline
performance.basis: depends on size and coating quality

source.note: Wikipedia, Cathodic protection, read 25 October 2026 (secondary source)

performance.metric: cathodic protection criterion for buried steel pipelines
performance.unit: mV vs copper/copper-sulfate electrode (CSE), polarised potential
performance.basis: the standard criterion of -850 mV vs CSE "can provide full protection for a buried API 5L" steel per NACE/AMPP SP0169 practice (critical-review paper: "the optimum potential is -850 mV for both steels"); SP0169 also allows a 100 mV cathodic-polarisation criterion and bounds overprotection near -1150 mV; FBE/3LPE coating property tables were not captured this pass

source.note: Cathodic protection criteria paper (ResearchGate record, read 2026-10-28); NACE SP0169 criteria as summarised

limitations: Disbonded shielding coatings can hide corrosion from CP
